shots.action: A locked-off view of the side window of a moving city bus at night. Rain streams down the glass in wavering threads and fattening beads, dragging the smeared reflections of streetlights and passing headlights into long wobbling streaks across the dark pane. Beyond the wet glass the street outside slides past as soft, out-of-focus pools of amber and pale blue light; inside the frame the window frame and a strip of worn bus interior trim hold steady. Droplets cling, swell and release, each one leaving a fresh wet track down the pane as the vehicle hums along.

shots.action: The same locked camera holds on the bus window, now seen much closer, so the glass fills the frame. Within each droplet the night street is bent into a tiny curved image of amber lamps and red tail lights, flipping and stretching as the drops slide. Behind the pane the deeper darkness of the bus interior is almost flat, and the wet glass breathes with a faint tremble from the road.
shots.what_changes: Droplets merge and break loose, carving new channels down the glass as their mirrored street lights warp and slip sideways.

description.text: At night, rain streams down the side window of a moving city bus in wavering threads and swelling beads. The wet glass drags smeared reflections of streetlights and passing headlights into long, trembling streaks across the dark pane. Beyond the window, out-of-focus pools of amber and pale blue light slide past while the dark interior window frame and a strip of worn trim hold steady around the glass. Droplets cling, swell, and release, each leaving a fresh track as the bus carries the pane steadily along.
Steady rain patters and ticks against the glass under a low engine hum.
A faint wet hiss rises from the tyres outside.
The camera holds a static shot.

The same bus window is seen much closer, so the rain-filled glass fills the view. Individual water beads stand sharp against the dark beyond, some trembling in place while others join and merge into heavier drops that break loose and cut crooked vertical channels through the film of water. Within each droplet the night street is bent into a tiny curved image of amber lamps and red tail lights, flipping and stretching as the drops slide. Behind the pane the deeper darkness of the bus interior is almost flat, and the wet glass shivers faintly with the road.
Close raindrops tick delicately against the glass.
The bus engine rumbles low beneath the window.
The camera holds a static shot.

The rain-streaked bus window remains in view as the downpour thickens and then eases. Sheets of water sweep across the pane in a quick gust, blurring the night outside into running bands of colour, before the flow thins to scattered slow trickles that hesitate and stop. The last few drops hang heavy and still on the glass, holding small steady points of amber light, while the dark street and its drifting reflections settle behind them. Nothing in the scene moves except the water on the window and the far-off lights sliding gently past.
Rain briefly thickens to a heavier patter on the glass.
The patter eases into sparse single ticks as the engine hum continues.
The camera holds a static shot.
